scope: Reusable native substitutions, displacements and traversal correspondences, with bounded recurrence search over the 18 authored atlas readings. This is an executable symmetry study, not autonomous concept discovery, a global minimum-description search, material transfer or geometric settlement.

bitGrammar.name: Exchange axes
bitGrammar.meaning: Choose V as the image of H, and H as the image of V.

bitGrammar.name: Oppose H image
bitGrammar.meaning: Reverse the ordered target direction selected for input H.

bitGrammar.name: Oppose V image
bitGrammar.meaning: Reverse the ordered target direction selected for input V.

bitGrammar.name: Reverse traversal
bitGrammar.meaning: Reverse the section order and each section's endpoint order, independently of the basis action.

tReadings.name: Two open T-shaped boundaries
tReadings.note: Seven-edge windows share three actual source sections. The transformed copy predicts the second window; the original overlapping reads reference one path. These are open T-shaped outlines, not three-way native junctions.

tReadings.name: Two decorated T-shaped boundaries
tReadings.note: Fifteen-edge windows share seven actual source sections. The curled flanges belong to a decorated T/corridor read. Literal T contacts against the framing rail are a separate projected read; their native course and rail are not welded.

controls.name: A reflection predicts the directed path
controls.note: Horizontal steps are unchanged; vertical steps reverse. Source and copy have independent site identities with the same alias pattern.

controls.name: Same turns; different reach
controls.note: The reflected action misses one changed reach. Similar turn order is weaker than exact correspondence; no settlement silently repairs it.

controls.name: Same coordinates; broken handoffs
controls.note: The support matches, but each section has independent endpoints. Coordinate equality does not prove path continuity.

controls.name: Same support; reversed traversal
controls.note: Reflection alone cannot explain the target's order. A support-only read would lose this distinction.

controls.name: Reflection and reversal together
controls.note: Adding the separate traversal correspondence accounts for the reversed target without changing the basis law.

findings: A2 and B6 admit overlapping boundary readings produced by vertical reflection plus advance. Shared source sections are one piece of evidence read twice, not duplicate material.
Vertical reflection changes vertical direction in the selected frame; it does not itself reverse horizontal motion. Reversing traversal changes both the order and each directed section.
One small instruction can describe a witnessed correspondence and generate a fresh copy on a different input. The application and match still retain separate evidence.
The smallest tested seed is conditional on this grammar and on the chosen realization. It is not an original-engine probability or a complete storage-cost estimate.
Topology, ordered motion, equal reaches, geometric support and projected crossings are different invariants. A shared silhouette does not imply shared routes or physical junctions.

A desired rectangle or hexagon can next be a connected target claim. Turning mismatch into change still needs explicit response routes, movable parameters, resistance and retained unresolved tension; this study does not add an unseen shape solver.
